coverageNote: Enumeration from disk matched the expected 7 units / 39 files exactly. Units are the domain directory itself plus the six sub-domain directories (12.01-12.06), each containing an *-index.md. No directory lacked an index. Every one of the 39 files was read in full. Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is scored only on the domain-root unit, whose index names four competitors (DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby, Vydia) with a specific capability gap and a defensible moat; it is N/A on the six sub-domain units, where competitive framing is not in scope and lives in meta/competitive-landscape.md.
scoringMethod: Dimension scores follow the vision-rubric's own stated criteria for the ✅/⚠️/❌ bands. Finding severity is recorded independently of the dimension band, so a blocking contradiction does not inflate a dimension whose ❌ criterion ('major features absent') is not met.

12.01.02:153 'stores default to all certified' vs 12.01.01:68 'If no stores have been selected yet ... union of all available stores' — reconciled by 12.03.01:38 (default = every certified store) plus 12.03.01:265 (deselect-all is a reachable state), so the union branch is reachable rather than dead.

findings.claim: 12.08 states in Behavior that imported ISRC retention is settled and unconditional, then states in its own Happy Path that retention is conditional on the prefix — two statements about the same fact that cannot both hold, with no marker on either.
findings.evidence: 12.08-catalog-migration-exit.md:36-39 — "The **ISRC half is settled**: imported ISRCs are kept whatever prefix they came from — 12.07 D-01 ... Nothing here is pending." vs 12.08-catalog-migration-exit.md:76 — "ISRCs are retained where the prefix allows; original release date is preserved in metadata where stores permit."
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building migration-in reads Happy-Path step 3, looks for the prefix-eligibility rule that gates retention, and finds none anywhere in the tree (12.07 rule 2 says a recording carrying an ISRC 'from any prefix' is never reassigned). Implementer A retains unconditionally per line 36; implementer B invents a prefix-eligibility predicate and drops ISRCs that fail it, minting duplicate ISRCs on migrated catalog — the permanent data error 12.07 DT-02 exists to prevent.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a prefix condition gates retention of imported ISRCs at all, and if so what it is.

findings.claim: A partner-suspension `Held` has no state or mapping in the per-store status board, which owns the status object — two sibling features specify `Held` with mandated artist-facing copy, and 12.03.02 resolves the neighbouring `Failed` case explicitly while never mentioning `Held`.
findings.evidence: 12.02.03-delivery-choreography-acknowledgement.md:302 — "| Held | Partner suspended, endpoint down, or our credential lapsed | **no equivalent — gap** | \"Held, not lost\" + honest attribution (D-06) |"; 12.02.03:335 — "this feature's `Failed` and `Held` states have **no equivalent** in 12.03.02's board vocabulary — a credential lapse currently has nowhere honest to land"; 12.04.01-release-date-lead-time.md:327 — "| Held | Window reached, gate not green (§8) | Dispatch held, date retained, person named, options enumerated. |"; 12.03.02-per-store-delivery-status.md:44-55 (state vocabulary: Queued, Sent, Received, Accepted, Live (pre-order), Live, Rejected, Withdrawn, Removed by store, Unknown — no Held); 12.03.02:110 resolves the sibling case — "Transport failure is not a state here — it is 12.02.03's `Failed` and stays `Sent` on the board until it resolves"; 12.03.02:100-103 assigns itself the reconciliation — "This feature owns the status object (CX-02), so the refinement is made here ... 12.02.03's vocabulary and this one must be reconciled as one vocabulary during synthesis, not two."
findings.failureScenario: A partner's credentials expire (12.02.02 D-10 / `Suspended`, a routine event that also fires on a lapsed contract or a missed deprecation deadline). Every queued release for that partner is held. Implementer A renders the row `Queued`, whose documented affordance is 'change the schedule' — wrong action, and it drops 12.02.03 D-06's mandatory honest attribution of fault (ours vs theirs). Implementer B renders `Sent · overdue`, which blames the partner for our credential lapse — the exact inversion D-06 forbids. Implementer C adds a `Held` state the board spec does not define, and 12.03.02 D-09's four-trigger interrupt rule has no entry for it.
findings.forcedInvention: The artist-facing board state for a suspended partner, its legal transitions, and whether it earns an interrupt.

findings.claim: 12.08's what-leaves table still has only two identifier rows and conflates ISRC with UPC, although 12.07 records both corrections as owed to it and its own Q-01 text contradicts the table it sits beside.
findings.evidence: 12.08-catalog-migration-exit.md:53-54 — "| ISRC/UPC from **their** prefix | ✅ Theirs | 12.07 D-02 |" and "| ISRC/UPC from **our** prefix | ⚠️ The whole question | See DT-02 |"; 12.07-identifier-assignment-at-delivery.md:259 — "**Two corrections this feature owes 12.08**: its exit table needs a third row for third-party prefixes (DT-12), and its single \"ISRC/UPC from our prefix\" row conflates two identifiers whose exit answers differ (DT-05, Q-03)"; 12.07 DT-12:249 — "**there is a third value, and it is common** ... This is a live break in 12.08's model — the exit table has rows for \"their prefix\" and \"our prefix\" and no row for \"someone else's\", which is the row a Producer-run label produces every time"; 12.07 D-07:281 — "**ISRC and UPC have separate policies** — for allocation, provenance and exit"; 12.08 Q-01:163 — "this row decides ISRC only", which the table row does not say.
findings.failureScenario: An artist departs holding a catalogue whose ISRCs came from a prior distributor's prefix or from a Producer-run label's prefix (12.07 D-13's third value, described as common and produced by all migrated catalogue). The exit manifest computation has no row for that class, and the row it does have answers ISRC and UPC together where 12.07 D-07 says they must diverge. Implementers differ on whether a third-party-prefix identifier leaves, and on whether the UPC answer follows the ISRC one.
findings.forcedInvention: The exit disposition for a third-party-prefix identifier, and whether the UPC half follows the ISRC half.

findings.claim: The required four-value source list for a supplied identifier has no defined mapping onto D-13's three-value prefix provenance, and the artist's-own-label case is pulled in opposite directions by two parts of the same file.
findings.evidence: 12.07-identifier-assignment-at-delivery.md:121-124 — "A **source is required** before save, from a closed list: *my registrant prefix* / *my label's prefix* / *issued by a prior distributor* / *from an existing release of this recording*. The answer is recorded as the provenance of the claim"; 12.07 D-13:287 — "Prefix provenance is **three-valued** (ours / the artist's / a third party's) and recorded **per recording, never per release**"; Role Lens:24 treats a label prefix as something the Musician already holds — "their own registrant prefix, their label's, or one issued by a prior distributor"; Cross-Cut Notes:266 pulls the other way — "the third-party-prefix case (DT-12) is a *label entity* from 01 holding a registrant code, distinct from the human who supplied it".
findings.failureScenario: An artist who runs their own label supplies an ISRC and selects 'my label's prefix'. Implementer A records provenance = the artist's (per the Role Lens grouping); implementer B records provenance = a third party's (per the 01 label-entity reasoning). The value is displayed to the artist, is stated 'in exit terms at the moment it is set' (12.07:150), and selects which 12.08 exit row applies — so the two implementations tell the artist different things about what leaves with them.
findings.forcedInvention: Which of the three provenance values each of the four source-list answers yields.

findings.claim: The readiness gate declares its condition set exhaustive, but two sibling features route blocking conditions into it that no condition family contains — so the routed blocks land nowhere.
findings.evidence: 12.01.03-delivery-readiness-gate.md:56-57 — "**Conditions** are the gate's own: social checks over facts other humans own. These are enumerated exhaustively below." (Families A-E, plus an explicit 'What is deliberately NOT a condition' table listing five exclusions, none of them label copy or territory). Routed in anyway: 12.01.05-label-copy-distributor-of-record.md:82 — "| No release year available yet | (P)/(C) year cannot derive; field left empty and flagged at the readiness gate (12.01.03) |" and 12.01.05:92 — "| Empty | No ownership record in 09 | Blocking — routes to the readiness gate (12.01.03) rather than asking for free text here |"; 12.03.01-store-selection-territory-scoping.md:403 D-04 — "Missing territory data blocks and routes to the gate; it never defaults to worldwide" (also :255, :300).
findings.failureScenario: A release reaches delivery with no territory data in 09 and an empty (P)-line year. An implementer building the gate from 12.01.03's exhaustive taxonomy produces Families A-E only, so neither block exists and the release proceeds to generation, where 12.02.01 fails on an absent Deal class and records it as a gate escape. An implementer who instead adds them to the gate has changed their semantics: per 12.01.03 D-06 conditions gate *delivery* and are social/chaseable, whereas both of these are author-fixable in seconds and belong to validation, which gates *presentation* — and 12.01 CX-02 forbids the two sharing a surface.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a missing (P)/(C) year, an absent 09 ownership record and absent territory data are gate conditions or validation findings.

findings.claim: The audio upload size ceiling is an unfilled placeholder in artist-facing copy, in a file that otherwise fixes every threshold it uses.
findings.evidence: 12.01.04-audio-artwork-asset-conformance.md:187 — "| Upload exceeds the size ceiling | Rejected at the boundary, before bytes are stored or analysed | \"This file is 4.2 GB. The ceiling is {N} GB — if that's an Atmos deliverable it goes in the spatial slot.\" |"; the enforcement is normative at :186 — "Size and decoded-dimension ceilings are enforced *before* any decode"; no value appears anywhere in the file, and no Open Question covers it (Q-01 storage, Q-02 Atmos resolved, Q-03 fingerprint resolved, Q-04 statutory scanning, Q-05 artwork variants). Contrast the same file's explicit values: "≥ 3000 × 3000 px", "under −60 dBFS", "3 attempts, exponential backoff at 30 s / 2 min / 8 min", "under 3 seconds".
findings.failureScenario: A Producer uploads a multi-GB 24/96 album master from a studio uplink (the file's own DT-12 sizes this as normal). Implementer A sets 2 GB and rejects legitimate masters at the boundary before any analysis; implementer B sets 20 GB and accepts decompression-bomb payloads the same edge-case row is written to stop. The rejection message quotes a ceiling the spec never fixes.
findings.forcedInvention: The per-file upload size ceiling that gates acceptance and appears in the artist-facing rejection.

findings.claim: 12.02.03 still declares three board-vocabulary gaps as open, one of which has since been closed by an owner ratification the file was never reconciled with — so it now asserts the opposite of the ratified model.
findings.evidence: 12.02.03-delivery-choreography-acknowledgement.md:298 — "| Partially accepted | Ack: `partially-accepted` (DT-07) | **no equivalent — gap** |" and :96 — "| `partially-accepted` | Release accepted, ≥1 track rejected (DT-07) | Board has no equivalent — see Cross-Cut Notes |", against 12.03-dsp-store-territory-management-index.md:71 D-05 — "Mixed track outcomes use **attached rejected-item details** under the existing `(release × store × territory)` status identity | Owner ratification for A-05 / `r-54[1]`, 2026-07-20" and 12.03.02-per-store-delivery-status.md:70 — "The parent projects `Partial acceptance` while evidence remains mixed" (D-18:392). The sibling `Failed` gap is likewise closed at 12.03.02:110 while 12.02.03:301 still calls it "**no equivalent — gap**".
findings.failureScenario: An implementer taking 12.02.03 as the authority on what the board can express builds a partial-acceptance path with no board representation — either collapsing the row to `Accepted` (concealing that the album is now 11 tracks) or to `Rejected` (concealing that 11 tracks ship on Friday), both of which the file itself calls lies, and both of which contradict the ratified rejected-item-detail model.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the board can represent partial acceptance, and which of the two conflicting models to build.

findings.claim: The gate requires a disputed credit to be withheld from the delivered ERN, but the generator spec — sole owner of what is projected — never carries the rule and its stated doctrine points the other way.
findings.evidence: 12.01.03-delivery-readiness-gate.md:84 B-3 — "The contested credit is withheld from the delivered metadata (ERN 12.02.01, RIN 02.08) until resolved; everything else ships." Against 12.02.01-ern-message-generation.md:72 — "| **Resources** | Each recording: ... contributors and their roles ... | 02 (credits/roles) | **Block** (DT-01) |", :210 D-01 — "Generation is a pure projection; nothing is defaulted or authored", and :219 D-10 — "Every contributor role is projected; a person is never collapsed to a primary role". No edge case, fact-class note, decision or open question in 12.02.01 mentions dispute-withholding.
findings.failureScenario: A credit dispute (02.05) is open on a named contributor when the delivery window arrives. Implementer A projects all credits (per D-01/D-10, since generation authors nothing and no filter is specified), publishing a contested claim to every DSP — which the gate's B-3 rationale calls 'claiming more than we know'. Implementer B filters the disputed credit, making the generator a selective author of the credit set, which D-01 forbids, and must invent where the filter lives (02's projection, generation, or the profile).
findings.forcedInvention: Whether and where a credit under active dispute is filtered out of the ERN.

findings.claim: A sub-domain open question carries a pipeline stage in its Owner column instead of an owner, so no party is accountable for answering it.
findings.evidence: 12.02-ddex-delivery-messaging-index.md:75 — "| Q-02 | Which **ERN version(s)**? ERN 4.x is current; large partners still consume 3.8.2. Direct delivery means supporting both. | `/create-prd` | `/create-prd-architecture` |". Every other open question in the unit names a person-class owner: Q-01 "| User | `/create-prd` |", Q-03 "| Agent | ✅ Resolved"; 12.02.01 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 all "| User |"; 12.02.02 Q-01..Q-07 all User or Agent.
findings.failureScenario: The ERN-version decision is load-bearing for 12.02.02 PC-02 and for the profile resolution key (12.02.02 D-11, which includes ERN version). With a stage in the owner slot, `/create-prd` receives a question whose owner is itself, and `/create-prd-architecture` receives a question nobody was assigned to bring; it passes both gates unanswered exactly as the domain's other expired deferrals did.
findings.forcedInvention: Who decides the supported ERN version set.

findings.claim: A ratified decision that only verified artist IDs are emitted for delivery contradicts the tier table's statement that Tier-B IDs can be emitted — and Tier B is defined as having no verification path, so under the decision no Tier-B ID can ever be emitted.
findings.evidence: 12.03.04-artist-profile-linking-disambiguation.md:135 D-05 — "Links are typed **verified** (Tier-A claim/auth) vs **asserted** (Tier-B); **only verified IDs are emitted for delivery**, asserted-but-unverifiable links are flagged to Trust & Safety (24)"; state table :101 — "| Unverified | A Tier-A link was asserted but not claimed | \"Claim this page to use it for delivery\" — not emitted until verified |". Against the tier definition :60 — "| B — addressable, not claimable | Store accepts an artist ID in the ERN but has no self-serve claim/verify path | The ID can be emitted and held, but ownership is **asserted, not proven** — see D-05 |". Q-04 :144 presupposes emission is available — "what is the acceptable evidence bar before an asserted link is treated as trusted enough to emit — or are Tier-B links always emitted-with-warning?"
findings.failureScenario: A Tier-B store is selected. Implementer A follows D-05 and emits no artist ID, so the store name-matches — reintroducing the wrong-page/duplicate-page disaster this feature exists to prevent (:38-43), on the class of store least able to recover from it. Implementer B follows the tier row and emits the asserted ID, which D-05 forbids and which the file's own hijack edge case (:88) treats as an impersonation surface.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether Tier-B asserted IDs are emitted for delivery at all, pending Q-04's evidence bar.

findings.claim: A decision guarantees that pre-saves survive a release date change, while the sub-domain CX says the guarantee is not the platform's to give and 12.04.01's own edge case describes it failing.
findings.evidence: 12.04.03-pre-save-pre-add-links.md:107 D-04 — "| D-04 | Pre-saves survive a release date change | A date move is not the fan's fault |" (restated :64 — "Pre-saves **must survive it**"). Against 12.04-release-scheduling-windows-cx.md:80 — "The pre-save grant lives at the DSP, not with us — we cannot re-point what we do not hold. Whether a store's pre-save survives a date change is **the store's behaviour, not our decision**, which means D-04 in 12.04.03 ('pre-saves survive a date change') may be an intention we cannot actually honour. That needs confirming per store before it is stated to artists. `[PENDING — Step 5]`"; and 12.04.01-release-date-lead-time.md:289 — "| Date moved earlier while pre-saves exist | **The worst case in the sub-domain** ... the pre-save fires against nothing | \"Pulling this forward risks every pre-save on Spotify firing against a record that isn't there yet. We can't undo that for your fans.\" |"
findings.failureScenario: An artist moves an announced date. Implementer A implements D-04 as a requirement and shows the artist 'your pre-saves carry' — a promise the DSP, not WeJammin, controls, and one that is false in the moved-earlier case. Implementer B implements 12.04.01's warning and tells the artist pre-saves may be lost. On the only fan-facing surface in domain 12, the product either over-claims or contradicts its own decision.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether pre-save survival across a date change is a platform guarantee, a per-store capability, or a warning.

findings.claim: A store accepting and then rejecting retracts both the editorial pitch and the pre-save link, and this is recorded as unhandled behind an ownerless deferral to a stage that has already closed — while the transition it depends on is explicitly legal elsewhere.
findings.evidence: 12.04-release-scheduling-windows-cx.md:68 — "5. **State transition conflict**: A store accepting and then rejecting on re-review would retract both. Rare, real, and unhandled. `[PENDING — Step 5]`" (no owner, and Step 5 is complete per ideation-index.md D-23/D-24). The transition is normal: 12.03.02-per-store-delivery-status.md:112 — "**`Accepted` → `Rejected` is legal** — stores reject at QC after accepting a delivery" and :291 — "| **Accepted then rejected** (QC after acceptance) | Legal transition." Neither 12.04.02 (states :67-76) nor 12.04.03 (states :72-79) carries a retraction state, and no open question in the unit covers it.
findings.failureScenario: Apple accepts, the pitch is submitted inside the window and the pre-save link is live and circulating to fans; Apple then rejects at QC. Nothing specifies whether the pitch is withdrawn or silently dead, whether the pre-save link keeps resolving, or whether the fans who already granted an OAuth scope are told. Implementers diverge on all three, and the OAuth grant obtained for a release that will not ship on that store has no defined disposal path.
findings.forcedInvention: What happens to a submitted pitch, a live pre-save link and existing fan grants when acceptance is retracted.

findings.claim: Recovery from an update that decomposes into takedown-plus-redeliver and fails between the two legs is unspecified, although the sub-domain CX names it the worst available outcome.
findings.evidence: 12.05-catalog-lifecycle-after-release-cx.md:62 — "an update that decomposes into takedown+redeliver must be atomic in intent — a failure between the two halves leaves the release down and not back up, which is the worst outcome available in this sub-domain"; :63 — "The second path can fail halfway. Recovery is `[PENDING — Step 5]` and matters more than its obscurity suggests." 12.05.02-metadata-update-redelivery.md specifies the path (:59-60 "*redeliver* (takedown + re-upload...)", :67-68) but its edge-case table (:95-106) and states (:110-119) contain no half-failed case, and neither Q-01 nor Q-02 covers it.
findings.failureScenario: An artist fixes a title on a store that requires takedown+redeliver. The takedown lands; the redelivery fails (rejection, transport fault, or a rule-pack change in between). The release is off that store with no specified state, no specified retry semantics, and no specified artist-facing statement — the artist's record is silently missing from a store after an action they were told was an edit.
findings.forcedInvention: The state, retry policy and artist-facing statement when the redeliver leg of a decomposed update fails after the takedown leg succeeded.

findings.claim: A Producer holds Config on updates and Read-only on takedown, so an update that decomposes into a takedown lets them effect a removal they have no permission to request — a hole the CX names plainly and neither feature file resolves or tracks.
findings.evidence: 12.05-catalog-lifecycle-after-release-cx.md:64 — "a Producer has `Config` on updates and `Read-only` on takedown. If their update silently decomposes into a takedown on some store, they have effected a removal they had no permission to request. **That is a real hole** and it follows directly from the shared machinery." The two permissions are as stated: 12.05-catalog-lifecycle-after-release-index.md:38-39 ("12.05.01 Voluntary Takedown | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only", "12.05.02 Metadata Update & Redelivery | ✅ Full | ⚙️ Config"). 12.05.02's Producer row (:27) grants asset-driven updates, and 12.01.04 D-10 (:261) establishes that replacing live audio "is often takedown + new ISRC" — the decomposing case. No decision or open question in 12.05.01, 12.05.02 or 12.05.03 addresses it.
findings.failureScenario: A Producer replaces a live master to fix a mix. On the stores that require takedown+new-ISRC, their Config-scoped update removes the release and forfeits streams, playlist position and the original release date — an act 12.05.01 gives them no permission to request and whose loss statement (12.05.01 D-01) is addressed to the owner. Implementers must invent whether Config covers redeliver-class changes, whether owner confirmation is required, or whether the Producer path is blocked per store.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a Producer's Config on updates extends to changes that decompose into a takedown, and what confirmation is required.

findings.claim: The resolving-update carve-out during suspension is called the sub-domain's most interesting unresolved question and given a leaning, while the feature file implements the opposite as a blanket rule — with no open question anywhere reconciling them.
findings.evidence: 12.05-catalog-lifecycle-after-release-cx.md:70 — "Some claims are resolved by an update ... CX-01 blocks exactly that. So the platform's safety mechanism can prevent the resolution it is waiting for."; :80 — "Leaning: allow **additive evidence** (clearances, credits, attestations) during suspension; block **mutations** of the claimed facts. That distinction is worth carrying to Step 5."; :31 — "The unresolved question is whether a **claim-resolving** update is exempt (CX-04)." Against the implemented rule: 12.05.02-metadata-update-redelivery.md:102 — "| Involuntary takedown active (12.05.03) | Updates blocked while unresolved | \"This release is suspended. Fix the dispute first.\" |" and :118 ("| Blocked | Involuntary takedown active |"), plus 12.05.03-involuntary-takedown-suspension.md:75 — "| Suspension while an update is in flight | Update frozen |". No Q row in 12.05.02, 12.05.03 or the sub-domain index carries the carve-out; Step 5 is complete (ideation-index.md D-23/D-24).
findings.failureScenario: An ownership claim is filed because a credit was missed. The fix is to add the credit — which the blanket freeze blocks. The artist's only route becomes the slower dispute process for a claim they concede, which the CX identifies as pure waste. An implementer following the CX's leaning builds an additive-evidence exemption; one following 12.05.02 builds the blanket block. The two produce opposite behaviour on the most distressing screen in the domain.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether additive-evidence updates are exempt from the suspension freeze.

findings.claim: Whether the derived claim whitelist re-derives after registration is left to an ownerless marker pointing at a closed stage, and the CX states outright that nothing reconciles the divergence — while the late-credit path that causes it is a specified, encouraged action elsewhere.
findings.evidence: 12.06-content-id-ugc-claiming-cx.md:33 — "the whitelist is a projection that can go stale when a band's line-up changes or a contributor is added late (12.05.02 DT-02). Whether it re-derives is `[PENDING — Step 5]` and matters"; :37 — "A contributor added to the credits *after* registration (the late-credit path, 12.05.02 DT-02) is not on the derived whitelist and may already have been claimed. The two features' timelines diverge and nothing currently reconciles them." The causing path is not hypothetical: 12.05.02 D-02 (:147) makes late credits "the cheapest, most encouraged action". 12.06.02's decisions (:105-108) and open questions (:114-115, both on claiming fans) do not cover re-derivation, and unlike 12.06.01 Q-02 — which honestly re-targets its expired deferral — this one is not re-targeted.
findings.failureScenario: A drummer's credit is added to a two-year-old record (the encouraged provenance win). They are not on the whitelist derived at registration time, so the automated claim machine claims their own session footage — the exact 'claim against your own drummer' outcome 12.06.02 D-02 exists to prevent, arriving through a path the product actively encourages. Implementers differ on whether the whitelist re-derives on credit change, on registration only, or never.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether and when the derived whitelist re-derives, and what happens to claims already made against a newly credited contributor.
